lines: Open the saved route in Edit and check its Name and Description
before changing its state.
This is the fictional Community supply loop from the route-planning lesson.
It has two prepared stops.
Unit still says Assign at start time, and Status is Draft.
Practice in a separate training department.
Before using a real plan, verify its locations, contacts and directions with
the people responsible for the work.
Change Status from Draft to Active.
Scroll to the bottom and select Save Changes.
The returned Routes list shows Active beside Community supply loop,
and its Actions now include Start.
The plan is ready for the start operation, but this saved status alone
does not show a unit executing it.
The next step explicitly chooses the unit and creates that execution.
Select Start on the saved route row.
The Start Route page asks for Assign Unit and says to select the
unit that will execute this route.
Choose the fictional Community van from the dropdown.
Review the route name and this unit selection together.
In your department, choose the resource responsible for these stops.
The Start Route Now button is the action that begins the execution;
Cancel leaves this start form.
Select Start Route Now once.
The returned Route Instance page shows In Progress in Instance Info, the
unit identifier, and a Started time.
Here the selected training van is represented by unit number
fifty-one thousand eight.
Ended is a dash, and Progress is zero of two.
These saved instance details show that the start succeeded.
They do not say that either service stop has already been completed.
Scroll down to inspect Stop Timeline.
Both entries are Pending in this newly started instance, and the
progress remains zero of two.
Use the status text and progress together when reviewing a route.
This recording has not checked into either location, and the map does
not display a generated road route.
Starting an instance is an administration step; verify
navigation and actual field progress separately before relying on them.
Return to Routes and select In Progress in the top action bar.
The overview now contains the Community supply loop card, its unit number,
start time and zero-of-two stop count.
Select View Details on that card.
The same instance information returns with In Progress and the original start time.
This lets a supervisor find an executing route again without
starting another instance.
Return to Routes and select History on the Community supply loop row.
Route History lists the stored execution with Status, Unit,
Started, Ended and Stops columns.
In this exercise there is one In Progress row, a start time, no end
time and zero of two completed stops.
Detail opens that execution.
Use this history when checking which instance a progress report refers
to, rather than treating the plan status as the execution history.
For this training check, return to Start and select the same Community van while
its first instance is still in progress.
Select Start Route Now once.
Resgrid returns Unit already has an active route instance.
This refusal means the second start did not succeed.
Do not keep retrying that unit.
Review its existing route before deciding whether another appropriate resource
should take a different assignment.
Leave the refused start with Cancel, return to Routes and open History again.
The recorded result still has the original single In Progress instance
with zero of two stops completed.
Keep the distinction clear: prepare the plan, start the intended unit,
then inspect actual progress.
This pattern can support search-and-rescue logistics, security
service visits, wildland supplies, industrial response support, community
paramedicine or mental health outreach, as well as fire and E M S.
Match the stops and assigned resource to your department’s work.
